justifications.functional_suitability: All requirements are directly fulfilled: R-01 via Customer Portal, R-02 through Adjuster Workspace, and R-03 with Claim Routing Component and Routing & Policy Engine enabling incremental claim-type migrations.
justifications.performance_efficiency: The sub-2s target (R-05) against 5s mainframe latency is met using Read Model & Caching Component (Redis/Azure SQL), Performance Views, and asynchronous event offloading through Azure Service Bus.
justifications.compatibility: Mainframe Anti-Corruption Layer (ACL) Client, Mainframe Sync Adaptor Component, and APIM handle legacy DB2/COBOL coexistence. External Identity Provider integrates via MSAL.js and OIDC/SAML for enterprise Active Directory SSO.
justifications.usability: Customer Portal serves brokers and customers with tracking and uploads. Adjuster Workspace provides adjusters with keyboard navigation, optimistic UI, and Audit Banner Component. Migration Operator Dashboard serves risk operators.
justifications.reliability: Zero-loss and exactly-once processing (R-04) are enforced via Sync & Integration Module's outbox pattern, FIFO Legacy Sync Queue sessions, Polly resilience policies, and System Dead-Letter Sub-system.
justifications.security: R-07 SSO is enforced by Auth Integration Client and APIM token validation. System uses Azure Key Vault via Managed Identity, mTLS, VNet Private Endpoints, and cryptographic audit logs.
justifications.maintainability: One-day rollback (R-06) is guaranteed via Routing & Policy Engine, Claim Routing Component, and Migration Operator Dashboard. Clean boundaries are maintained via Mainframe Anti-Corruption Layer Client.
justifications.portability: Hybrid connectivity between azure-westeurope and on-prem-mainframe is well structured using APIM, Private Endpoints, and Hybrid Data Adapter, though high coupling to Azure proprietary PaaS services reduces multi-cloud replaceability.

PERF-01.justification: The architecture decouples UI reads from slow mainframe latency by using an asynchronous Sync Engine, replicated data in the Sync & Integration Module, and a dedicated Read Model & Caching Component backed by Redis and SQL performance views.
sensitivity_points: Cache invalidation latency versus data freshness requirements
Replication lag between mainframe changes and Azure SQL mirrored data
tradeoffs: Eventual consistency of mainframe claim data in exchange for sub-second UI response times

PERF-02.justification: Peak submission volumes are decoupled from backend processing via Azure Service Bus queuing, while rate-limiting and scheduled batch dispatching in the Integration Workers prevent unexpected workloads from overflowing into the mainframe batch window.
sensitivity_points: Service Bus queue ingestion throughput limits under peak burst conditions
Rate-limiter throttling thresholds configured on mainframe integration adapters
tradeoffs: Asynchronous submission acknowledgment improves intake capacity but delays confirmation of mainframe persistence

AVAIL-01.justification: Customer Portal and Backend APIs remain fully available during the batch window. Submissions are queued in Azure Service Bus and processed asynchronously by Integration Workers once the mainframe resumes operation after 05:00.
sensitivity_points: Azure Service Bus message retention limits and queue storage capacity
Circuit breaker configuration during scheduled mainframe downtime
tradeoffs: Accepting submissions while mainframe is offline delays end-to-end claim adjudication

AVAIL-02.justification: The design incorporates transactional outbox patterns, FIFO queue sessions keyed by Claim ID, idempotency tables, and a dedicated Reconciliation Worker to identify mismatched states and prevent duplicate or lost claims.
sensitivity_points: Strict idempotency enforcement across mainframe calls
Reconciliation schedule frequency versus detection lag
tradeoffs: Deduplication tracking and outbox table management introduce database write overhead

MOD-01.justification: Claim type migration and rollbacks are supported by dynamic feature flags in Azure App Configuration, content-based routing in the Claim Routing Component, and operational switch-back controls in the Migration Operator Dashboard.
sensitivity_points: Dynamic routing propagation speed across container instances
Data synchronization parity during bidirectional cutover and rollback
tradeoffs: Dual-routing code paths add operational complexity to backend APIs and queue listeners

MOD-02.justification: The frontends interface exclusively with Backend APIs and the Hybrid Data Adapter behind APIM. Decommissioning the mainframe requires updating routing configurations and disabling synchronization adapters without altering client application logic.
sensitivity_points: Total abstraction of legacy data formats behind modern domain entities
Removing synchronization dependencies without breaking shared schema contracts
tradeoffs: Maintaining facade adapters during migration incurs preliminary overhead to protect UI longevity

SEC-01.justification: APIM validates identity tokens and Customer Portal enforces authenticated sessions. However, fine-grained object-level authorization (verifying broker tenant ownership over requested claim IDs) is not explicitly detailed in backend service components.
sensitivity_points: Tenant context validation rules implemented in Backend APIs
Completeness of security audit log coverage for unauthorized access attempts
tradeoffs: Fine-grained data-level access checks on every request add minor compute latency

SEC-02.justification: While SSO is integrated with Active Directory, the architecture lacks explicit mechanisms for instant JWT token revocation or Continuous Access Evaluation (CAE), risking valid token use until standard token expiration occurs.
sensitivity_points: Access token TTL duration configured in Active Directory
Mechanisms to synchronize account deactivation instantly with mainframe access control
tradeoffs: Shorter token lifetimes improve revocation latency but increase authentication token refresh traffic
